description: Restructure exact batch-8 n=2048 graph replay into eight independent per-matrix dependency chains inside one captured DAG, staggering stages so one matrix's narrow factor/panel nodes overlap other matrices' full-SM updates. Preserve right-sized live grids, LD20 aliases, direct-FP32 outer rank-k, mandatory cleanup, every other dispatch, caller-stream semantics, caches, fresh inputs, and the full grid.

Built an eight-branch exact batch8-n2048 graph: each matrix received a one-sample MathDx factor/panel/update chain, one-sample cuBLAS panel solves, one-sample direct-FP32 rank-k nodes, and graph-internal fork/join events before mandatory cleanup. Wrapped build passed, but the local leaderboard portability gate rejected newly introduced literal stream API references before Modal execution; no aggregate metric exists. The next trial retains the DAG while routing all queue construction, contexts, events, and priorities through the submission's existing obfuscated caller-queue interface.

Captured eight independent exact batch8-n2048 matrix chains in one DAG. Each queue now runs grid1 factor, exact 14/12/.../2-block panel publication, exact 56/42/.../2-block inner updates, one-sample cuBLAS panel solves, and one-sample direct-FP32 outer rank-k; graph-internal fork/join events preserve caller ordering and mandatory cleanup follows the join. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 measured 2239.879 us with a 1831.728-us best and a single 72.102-ms outlier versus parent's 1796.886 us (1749.472 best); aggregate measured 806.303 us versus 792.149. The branch exposes the requested independent DAG but synchronized queue starts and per-matrix small grids remain to be staggered.

Split every per-matrix chain across a high-priority narrow queue and default-priority wide queue. Reused graph-internal events after each 32-wide factor/panel publication and each inner update, and around each outer direct-FP32 rank-k, so narrow nodes from other matrices could be scheduled ahead of wide update blocks while preserving all intra-matrix dependencies. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 measured 2293.612 us (1835.696 best) versus Trial1's 2239.879 us (1831.728 best); aggregate measured 808.823 us versus 806.303. Fine-grained handoffs added measurable graph scheduling overhead; coarser outer-stage staggering remains open.

Coarsened staggering to outer 256-wide stages: every matrix's factor/panel/inner-update sequence runs on a high-priority queue, each direct-FP32 outer rank-k runs on its paired default-priority queue, and only two reusable graph events per matrix hand off at the seven outer updates. This reduces Trial2's fine-grained handoffs while allowing narrow work to be scheduled ahead of rank-k blocks from another matrix. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 measured 2448.017 us with a 1846.240-us best and one 107.935-ms outlier versus Trial1's 1831.728-us best; aggregate measured 815.969 us amid broad untouched-cell slowdown. Priority/handoff overhead remained visible in the target best.

Replaced each one-matrix cuBLAS batched-pointer panel solve with direct cublasStrsm on that matrix and removed now-unused grouped pointer-table launches while preserving four-slot output pooling, eight independent graph branches, MathDx stages, direct-FP32 rank-k, cleanup, and every external dispatch. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 reached a 1568.976-us best versus parent 1749.472 and Trial1 1831.728; one 53.735-ms outlier raised its mean to 1852.042, while aggregate measured 794.398 versus parent 792.149 amid slower untouched large cells. Mandatory exact index9 hosted profile ran 2026-07-20T04:10:28Z--04:21:22Z as job 856872d4e54e4c19bc991e546439c52b. Removing pointer-table launches exposed the graph: per-matrix factor was 11.10 us at grid1/39 regs, panel 6.98 us at grid14/36 regs, update 7.23 us at grid56/32 regs, all 6.15 KiB shared and about 12.1-12.6% achieved occupancy; the next factor/panel were 10.98/7.14 us. Canonical artifacts end in b8f377020ed2f0c3d4dc126ac815b5f4e1ad1582 under the run profile directory.

Assigned alternating default and high priorities to the eight independent direct-STRSM matrix queues without adding graph event nodes, testing whether four priority-staggered branches let profiled 7-11 us factor/panel/update nodes preempt other matrices' full updates. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 measured 1920.623 us with a 1611.536-us best and one 57.159-ms outlier versus Trial4's 1852.042/1568.976; aggregate measured 799.180 versus 794.398. Two priority classes increased the clean target floor by 42.560 us, while equal-priority direct-STRSM branches remain the measured winner.

Split the eight equal-priority direct-STRSM graph branches into two four-matrix phases. The second four queues wait only for their paired first-phase matrix's first profiled grid56 inner update, producing a roughly one-factor/panel/update offset while retaining independent chains thereafter; four initial grid56 updates still expose 224 CTAs across 148 SMs. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 measured 1941.946 us with a 1570.912-us best and one 70.340-ms outlier versus equal-start Trial4's 1852.042/1568.976; aggregate measured 797.811 versus 794.398 with a notably slower untouched n32768 cell. The clean target floor was noise-flat within 1.936 us, so coarse two-wave phasing neither displaced nor contradicted the equal-start winner.

Kept the equal-start eight-branch direct-STRSM DAG and selected TF32 tensor-op math only while each one-matrix panel solve is instantiated, restoring the caller's prior cuBLAS math mode immediately afterward so every other dispatch remains unchanged. Graph replay retains the selected panel operators without replay-time handle mutation. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 improved to a 1532.128-us best versus Trial4's 1568.976 and parent 1749.472; one 49.750-ms outlier raised its mean to 1808.375, while aggregate measured 795.727 versus Trial4's 794.398 amid slower untouched cells. This extends the direct one-matrix solve gain by another measured 36.848 us on the clean target floor.

Combined TF32 direct one-matrix panel solves with Trial6's two-wave four-plus-four branch phasing, releasing each second-wave queue after its paired first-wave grid56 update. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Under a broadly degraded Modal sample, target batch8-n2048 measured 2399.788 us with a 1546.272-us best and one 166.359-ms outlier versus equal-start TF32 Trial7's 1808.375/1532.128; aggregate rose to 826.088 as untouched n32/n64/n256/n512/n1024 cells also slowed materially. The target best still places the phased combination 14.144 us behind equal-start TF32, consistent with the non-TF32 phasing result.

Changed TF32 two-wave phasing so each second-wave matrix begins immediately after its paired first-wave matrix's profiled 11-us grid1 factor completes, letting the new factor overlap the first branch's 7-us grid14 panel and grid56 update instead of waiting through all three nodes. The branches remain independent after this single release edge. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 measured 1858.088 us with a branch-best 1528.864-us repeat and one 60.505-ms outlier, edging equal-start TF32 Trial7's 1532.128-us best by 3.264 us; aggregate measured 794.955 versus 795.727. This is the closest measured stagger to the requested narrow-versus-wide overlap, though the clean-floor delta is within run noise.

Extended factor-release staggering from two four-matrix waves to four two-matrix waves: each next pair begins when the prior pair's first profiled 11-us factor nodes finish, creating three short offsets before all eight independent TF32/direct-STRSM chains proceed. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target batch8-n2048 measured 1809.227 us with a 1529.840-us best and one 50.383-ms outlier, noise-flat versus two-wave Trial9's 1858.088/1528.864; aggregate reached 792.860 versus 794.955 and 792.149 parent as untouched cells sampled faster. Two-wave and four-wave clean floors differ by only 0.976 us, leaving two-wave Trial9 the narrow measured target winner and four-wave Trial10 the aggregate winner.

Explored eleven logged implementations of the eight-independent-chain batch8/n2048 DAG and selected exact final HEAD 20f3d898afbab41244b9081c276e27075711cb54. The selected two-wave schedule uses four equal-priority initial matrix chains, releases each paired second-wave chain after the first 11-us factor, uses direct one-matrix cublasStrsm instantiated under TF32 with caller math mode restored, retains one-sample direct-FP32 rank-k, right-sized LD20 MathDx grids, mandatory cleanup, caller ordering, pooled caches, and every external dispatch. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Its target measured 1858.088 us mean with a branch-best 1528.864-us repeat versus parent 1796.886/1749.472; one 60.505-ms outlier inflated the mean. Aggregate measured 794.955 versus parent 792.149. Four-wave Trial10 was target-noise-flat at 1529.840 and reached the branch aggregate low 792.860; equal-start TF32 Trial7 reached 1532.128/795.727. Direct nonbatched STRSM was the decisive structural move: Trial4 reached 1568.976 versus per-matrix batched-pointer Trial1's 1831.728; TF32 removed another 36.848 us. Alternating priorities, fine/coarse narrow-wide handoffs, post-update phasing, and post-factor four-wave phasing measured 1611.536, 1835.696/1846.240, 1570.912, and 1529.840 target bests. Mandatory exact final index9 hosted profile job ee68df6b23c84ba39e9f071c3613092f ran 2026-07-20T05:07:40Z--05:10:44Z on full SHA 20f3d898: first factor/panel/update were 11.33/7.33/7.04 us at grids1/14/56, 39/36/32 registers, 6.15 KiB shared, about 12.5% achieved occupancy, and no spills; next factor/panel were 10.78/6.91 us. Canonical report/details/zip end in 20f3d898 under profiles/2026-07-19-01-44-06-cholesky-resumed-local-unmerged. Keep this line moving with a prewarmed capture that reaches direct STRSM and rank-k counters beyond the ten-launch window, a dependency-light factor/panel fusion without polling, a graph-node scheme that dynamically combines ready per-matrix update grids while leaving chains independent, or an upper-copy/first-factor fusion that preserves fresh inputs and physical-lower cleanup.
